defenses.reason: The exception handler on line 79 of the added code only catches ValueError. If task["due"] is not a string (e.g., null or an integer), re.fullmatch() in parse_date will raise TypeError on line 20 of core.py, which is not caught, causing an unhandled exception and traceback instead of the expected error handling.

defenses.quote: assert "1" in lines[0] and "soon" in lines[0]
defenses.reason: The assertion on line 261 is a bare substring check that would pass with any message containing "1" and "soon", such as "Position 1 has error: soon" or other formats that don't specifically verify the task id was correctly reported. The test does not enforce the exact format of the error message.

The test fixture on line 237 only creates a single open task with done: False. There is no test case that exercises the scenario of a done task with a malformed due date, or a mix of open and done tasks, so the guard `not task["done"]` on line 76 of cli.py is never tested with done tasks, and removing that guard would not be caught by this test.
